QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_23

question.text: An interest rate derivative whose value is based on the difference between two interest rates is called:

explanation.text: The Logic: An interest rate swap is an exchange of agreed interest payments on a notional principal. Such contracts generally involve fixed-to-floating or floating-to-floating interest rates, so the net settlement is driven by the difference between the two referenced rates. The Trap: Interest rate futures are exchange-traded contracts on an underlying interest rate, not a bilateral exchange of rate payments. "Contract for differences" is not the workbook's category for this product. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-IV workbook (Dec 2025), pages 94 and 101, which define interest rate swaps as fixed-to-floating or floating-to-floating exchanges of interest payments on a notional principal.
